characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.value:
Informed consent: quote "Written informed consent will be obtained by a qualified physician or nurse connected to the trial, prior to randomisation of any participant, unless the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) uses deferred informed consent or prior assent as consent methods (see below). These consent procedures will be approved by local ethics committees or institutional review boards." Further detail: https://www.nejm.org/doi/suppl/10.1056/NEJMoa2207554/suppl_file/nejmoa2207554_appendix.pdf

Ethics: quote "Before the trial launch, the protocol was approved by the relevant ethics committees at each trial site. An independent data and safety monitoring committee conducted one preplanned, blinded interim analysis after one third of the infants had reached 36 weeks’ postmenstrual age (data and safety monitoring are described in the Supplementary Appendix, available at NEJM.org). The trial was conducted in compliance with the International Council for Harmonisation guidelines for Good Clinical Practice, including local monitoring visits and central data monitoring conducted during the trial."

Inclusion criteria: 
Infants born with postmenstrual age less than 28 weeks
Signed informed consent, unless the NICU has chosen to use 'opt-out' or deferred consent as a consent method.

Exclusion criteria: 
Missing written parental informed consent (if the 'opt-out' method is used for consent, lack of a record that the clinical staff have explained the trial and the 'opt-out' consent process to parents and/or a record in the infant's clinical file of parents' decision to opt-out, are exclusion criteria)
Decision not to conduct full life support
No possibility to place cerebral NIRS oximeter within six hours after birth

Group differences: The characteristics of the infants were similar in the two groups

Total sample size: 1601

Withdrawals:  13 in NIRS group;  9 in NO NIRS group
Reasons for withdrawal: 

Mainly because of withdrawn informed consent.

The parents of 18 infants who were enroled under the terms of deferred consent did not eventually provide written informed consent and declined the use of their infants’ data. For three infants who were enroled under the terms of prior informed consent, the parents withdrew their consent and, for two of the three infants, also withdrew consent for the use of their infants’ data. Two infants from one site were lost to follow-up because the site withdrew from the trial shortly after the start of data collection.

Other: Serious adverse reactions included severe skin damage, physical injury associated with managing the device and sensors (critical displacement of endotracheal tubes or endovascular lines caused by cerebral oximetry monitoring), and clinical mismanagement (i.e., interventions aimed at improving respiratory or cardiovascular status and oxygen transport) that occurred on the basis of oximetry monitoring

risk-of-bias.support-for-judgement: Judgement Comment: "Infants will be centrally randomised to either the experimental or control group with a 1:1 allocation ratio at the Copenhagen Trial Unit using a web-based randomisation application."

Judgement Comment: "The allocation sequence will be computer-generated with varying block sizes concealed
for all investigators, as the web-based program will not release the randomisation until the patient has been included in the trial and stratified by NICU and gestational age group (lower gestational age (< 26 weeks) compared to higher gestational age (≥ 26 weeks)."

Judgement Comment: "The trial was analysed in accordance with a pre-specified plan.
Statistical analyses were conducted independently by two of the authors. The results of the
analyses were compared for discrepancies before unblinding; no significant discrepancies were
found.
All outcomes will be assessed at 36 weeks postmenstrual age: this assessment and data entry will be conducted by a person blinded to group allocation."
Judgement Comment: "some physicians of different NICUs didn't complete the training for getting a full adherence to RCT protocol"

Judgement Comment: "Withdrawal of patients was described: "The parents of 18 infants who were enrolled under the terms of deferred consent did not eventually provide written informed consent and declined the use of
their infants’ data. For three infants who were enrolled under the terms of prior informed con-
sent, the parents withdrew their consent and, for two of the three infants, also withdrew consent
for the use of their infants’ data. Two infants from one site were lost to follow-up because
the site withdrew from the trial shortly after the start of data collection"
The potential influence of missing data was assessed: " The results of the best–worst and worst–best case analyses and multiple imputation analyses showed that missing data did not have the potential to substantively affect results."
Nonadherence to the assigned intervention was described: "Nonadherence to the assigned intervention was documented in 36 of 772 infants (4.7%) in the oximetry group (who each had more than 14 hours of missing oximetry monitoring data) and in 20 of 807 infants (2.5%) in the usual-care
group (who underwent oximetry monitoring)""

Judgement Comment: "The outcome death was not blinded. Severe brain injury was performed in a blinded fashion but there was no central adjudication of cerebral ultrasound images. However, the diagnosis and classification of brain injury along with the entry of these data into the patient report form was conducted by an assessor blinded to study group allocation.
The data managers, statisticians, and those drawing conclusions were blinded to study group allocation. Assessments of other exploratory outcomes were not blinded."

- Decision to provide full life support 
- Possibility to start cerebral NIRS monitoring within three hours after birth
- Consent from the parents

Exclusion criteria: 

- A clinical decision not to provide full life support.
- No possibility to place the cerebral NIRS oximeter within 3 hours after birth.
- Lack of parental signed written informed consent.

Group differences: The baseline characteristics of the two groups were similar

Other: The variability in monitoring time was mainly due to death within the first three days of life (two infants were withdrawn from the trial by parental request and in four there were technical reasons for reduced NIRS recording time)

Judgement Comment: "The secondary outcome amplitude integrated electroencephalography has been reported separately in Pediatric Research 2016;79(4):528-35. [DOI: 10.1038/
pr.2015.266; PUBMED: 26679155]"

Judgement Comment: "The eight centres contributed 6, 8, 9, 11, 21, 36, 36, and 39 participants. The intervention effect showed significant heterogeneity amongst the centres (P<0.001). Removal of one centre with 36 infants resulted in the heterogeneity being insignificant (P=0.62). This centre had the largest reduction in
burden in the intervention group. A post hoc sensitivity analysis reducing the mean effect of the intervention in this centre to a value equal to the mean effect in the rest of the centres resulted
in a significant reduction in burden of 31% (P=0.0497)."

Judgement Comment: "Two infants in the control group did not have any NIRS data recorded; one had consent withdrawn and there were technical problems for the other.
All other data were collected per protocol for both."

Inclusion criteria: 

Neonates born more than 8 weeks preterm (gestational age up to 31 weeks and 6 days); decision to conduct full life support; parental informed consent; and cerebral NIRS oximeter placed within three minutes after birth.


Exclusion criteria: 

No decision to conduct full life support; no written informed consent; congenital malformation (including of the brain, heart, or lung, or the presence of prenatal cerebral injury).


Group differences: The personal and clinical characteristics of the mothers and infants did not differ between the groups, except for a higher number of foetuses with bradycardia in the near infrared spectroscopy group and a higher number of male infants in the control group, although both were of borderline significance 
(P=0.05 and P=0.06, respectively).


Total sample size: 655
Number of withdrawals: before birth: 9 in the intervention group and 5 in the control group after birth: 16 in the intervention group, 18 in the control group

Reason for withdrawal: 

14 were not included after birth as a research team was not available (9 in the intervention group and 5 in the control group).
24 were not included because parents declined deferred consent (13 in the intervention group and 11 in the control group).
7 not included for congenital malformation (3 in the intervention group and 4 in the control group)
2 lost to follow up (all in the control group)
1 excluded because parents withdrew consent (in the control group)

comment: low risk"

No other sources of bias

Judgement Comment: "16 patients were excluded in the intervention group: 13 because parents declined deferred consent and 3 for congenital malformation.
18 patients were excluded in the control group: 11 because parents declined deferred consent, 4 for congenital malformation, 2 were lost to follow up or had no cranial ultrasonograms, 1 because parents withdrew consent."

Judgement Comment: "Efforts were made to mask the clinical team in the neonatal intensive care unit—
especially to avoid recording the allocation group in the neonate’s chart.
However, cerebral ultrasonography was performed locally, and therefore
despite every effort, full masking to group allocation could not be guaranteed. "
